title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Credits usage report for pay-as-you-go in Copilot Chat
summary: The briefing passes: the report paths, API calls, prerequisites and preview limits are supported, including the updated Cost Management documentation. One minor correction is needed: Microsoft's notice expects rollout to finish by the end of May 2027 rather than guaranteeing completion.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on October 28, 2026.
The Microsoft Copilot Credits report shows total credits used for Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go consumption.
claims.quote:
This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies. It includes key metrics such as:
- Total credits used

claims.claim: The report includes a cumulative time series.
claims.quote: Cumulative and daily time series

claims.claim: The report includes a daily time series.

claims.claim: MC1069563 names Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption as the report path.
claims.quote: will be available in the Microsoft admin center at Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption:

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The current report path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote:
In the navigation menu, select Reports. If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports.
3. Select Usage.
4. On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.claim: The report appears after Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go is configured in either admin center and agent usage is enabled.
claims.quote: After you set up pay-as-you-go for Microsoft Copilot Chat, either in the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Power Platform admin center, and enable agent usage in your organization, you see a new report that includes metrics for credits used.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Consumption tab is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
2. Select the Consumption tab.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Consumption tab reports Copilot Credit usage by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote:
The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by:
- Spending policy
- User
- Group
- Agent
- Service

claims.claim: Learn does not present the Consumption tab as a replacement for the Copilot Chat Credits report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cost Management" "Copilot Chat" "report" replacement. Opened Monitor Copilot Credit spending, Microsoft Copilot Credits report, and Usage-based billing: What you see in the Microsoft 365 admin center vs. your Azure bill; no replacement statement found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage can take 24 hours to appear in Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: Billed amounts update daily, but usage can take up to 24 hours to appear in Azure Cost Management.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management is billing-oriented and lacks the same user-level and spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Shows billing-oriented cost data, such as costs by subscription, service, resource, meter, or invoice period. It doesn't show the same user-level or spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Credits report is not a general report of all Copilot Studio agent consumption.
claims.quote: The Credits used metric shows the total credits used from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter during the selected time period.

claims.claim: Eligible Copilot Chat consumption appears even when the billing policy is configured in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You can set up the pay-as-you-go billing policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center. If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usernames, display names, groups and sites are hidden by default in usage reports.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: The report's alert user details can be exported to CSV.

claims.claim: The documented example charges 10 credits for tenant graph grounding.
claims.quote: an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: The documented example adds two credits for generative answers.
claims.quote: 10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agent design influences the number of credits consumed.
claims.quote: The number of credits used depends on the design of the agent, how often users interact with it, and the features the agent uses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: MC1069563 says a Microsoft Copilot license is not required for this pay-as-you-go scenario.
claims.quote: This message refers to Microsoft Copilot in a pay-as-you-go model. A Microsoft Copilot license is not required.

claims.claim: A separate licensing model for the report itself is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "license" "price". Opened Microsoft Copilot Credits report, usage reports overview, and View costs and billing for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go; no separate report licence model was specified.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Credits report page states no separate price for the report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "license" "price". Read Microsoft Copilot Credits report in full and View costs and billing for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go; no separate charge for viewing the report was stated.

claims.claim: The report covers users without a Microsoft Copilot license interacting with Copilot Chat agents that use the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter

claims.claim: The report concerns metered Copilot Credit consumption under pay-as-you-go billing policies, rather than a report-viewing meter.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot Credits report helps you manage metered consumption costs for Microsoft Copilot Chat. This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.

claims.claim: The usage reports overview lists Copilot reports as unavailable in some government clouds.
claims.quote:
| Report | Public | GCC | GCC-High | DoD | Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet |
| Microsoft Copilot credits | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |

claims.claim: The tenant concealment setting is at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
Select Org Settings.
4. On the Services tab, select Reports.
5. In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings with { "displayConcealedNames": true } updates the tenant report concealment setting.
The listed Graph endpoints are beta APIs, for which production application use is not supported.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: displayConcealedNames true conceals user information and false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The report concealment setting also affects Billing Policy ID.
claims.quote: Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate} returns per-user credit consumption.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate=2026-07-01&endDate=2026-07-02&$orderby=consumedQuantity desc&$top=2&$count=true

claims.claim: The per-user Cost Management usage API requires exactly one completed UTC day per request.
claims.quote: The range must select exactly one completed UTC day. Current-day, future, and multi-day ranges are rejected, not clamped.

claims.claim: The per-user Cost Management usage API supports delegated work or school permissions only.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All | CopilotCostManagement.Read.All |
| Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported. |
| Application | Not supported. | Not supported. |

claims.claim: The per-user API is not equivalent to every Consumption tab breakdown or the dedicated Credits report.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementUserUsageRecord objects that report each user's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day, ranked by consumption.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose

claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Copilot Credits report API message consumption reports getCopilotCredits. Read Credits report and Cost Management userUsageRecords reference; search also returned Cost Management API overview, not an API for the dedicated report.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no additional report-specific administrative configuration beyond report access and concealment.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" configure settings API admin. Read Credits report, usage reports overview and adminReportSettings reference; results describe billing setup, roles, concealment and report viewing, not another report-specific administrative setting.
